Global warming is one of the most serious environmental challenges facing the world today. It refers to the gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth's atmosphere and oceans, mainly caused by human activities. Over the past few decades, the Earth's temperature has increased significantly due to the excessive release of greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide. These gases trap heat in the atmosphere, creating a phenomenon known as the greenhouse effect. Although the greenhouse effect is a natural process that helps maintain the Earth's temperature, human activities have intensified it, resulting in climate change and environmental imbalance.

One of the major causes of global warming is the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, petrol, diesel, and natural gas. These fuels are widely used in industries, vehicles, electricity generation, and transportation. When burned, they release large amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Deforestation is another important factor contributing to global warming. Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, but large-scale cutting of forests reduces the Earth's ability to absorb greenhouse gases. Industrial pollution, agricultural activities, excessive energy consumption, and improper waste management also contribute to the problem.

Global warming has several harmful effects on the environment and human life. One of the most visible impacts is the melting of glaciers and polar ice caps, which causes sea levels to rise. Rising sea levels threaten coastal cities and islands, increasing the risk of flooding and displacement of people. Another major effect is the increase in extreme weather events such as heatwaves, droughts, floods, cyclones, and unpredictable rainfall. Changes in temperature and rainfall patterns also affect agriculture, reducing crop production and creating food shortages in many regions. Animals and plants are also affected because their natural habitats are changing or disappearing. Some species may become endangered or extinct if they cannot adapt to these environmental changes.

Global warming also creates serious health problems. Increasing temperatures can cause heat exhaustion, dehydration, and heatstroke. Air pollution and changing weather conditions may worsen respiratory diseases and increase the spread of certain infections. People living in developing countries and economically weaker communities are often more vulnerable because they may have fewer resources to adapt to climate-related disasters.

However, global warming can be reduced through collective efforts by individuals, governments, and industries. Renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and hydropower should be encouraged instead of fossil fuels. Planting more trees, protecting forests, using public transportation, conserving electricity, and reducing plastic consumption can make a significant difference. Industries should adopt cleaner technologies and improve energy efficiency. Governments must introduce strict environmental regulations and promote sustainable development. Recycling and proper waste segregation can also help reduce pollution and unnecessary resource consumption.

In conclusion, global warming is not just an environmental issue but a global responsibility. Every individual has an important role in protecting the planet. Small actions, when performed collectively, can create meaningful changes. We must act responsibly today to ensure a cleaner, healthier, and safer planet for future generations. Protecting the Earth is not an option; it is our responsibility.

Temperature is a physical quantity that expresses the degree of hotness or coldness of a substance. The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin (K). In everyday life, temperature is commonly measured in degrees Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F). Absolute zero is 0 K or -273.15 °C. Heat is energy in transit that flows from a higher temperature body to a lower temperature body until thermal equilibrium is reached.

Check whether the zero marking of the main scale coincides with that of the zero of the vernier scale. If they coincide then there is no zero error. If they do not coincide with each other, the instrument is said to possess zero error which may be positive or negative. If the zero of a vernier lies to the right of the main scale zero, the error is positive. If the zero of vernier lies to the left of the main scale zero, then the error is negative. Always remember to correct the measured reading by subtracting the zero error with its proper algebraic sign.

It often becomes necessary in everyday life to express a quantity that is typical for a given data. Suppose a researcher says that on an average, people watch TV serials for 3 hours per day, it does not mean that everybody does so; some may watch more and some less. The average is an acceptable indicator of the data regarding programmes watched on TV. Averages summarise a large amount of data into a single value and indicate that there is some variability around this single value within the original data. A mathematician’s view of an average is slightly different from that of the commoner. There are three different definitions of average known as the Mean, Median and Mode. Each of them is found using different methods and when they are applied to the same set of original data they often result in different average values. It is important to figure out what each of these measures of average tells you about the original data and consider which one is the most appropriate to calculate.

text: Palaeoanthropologists and archaeologists excavate the soil and rock layers on the earth and extract evidence about human ancestors. These layers and the fossils are scientifically dated to study the various stages in human evolution and prehistory. Through the gathered evidence, they attempt to understand the evolution of human history and culture in a chronological order. The chimpanzees are genetically the closest to humans. The chimpanzees and other ancestral forms are together called the Hominins. The ancestors of humans evolved in Africa and then migrated to other parts of the world. They adapted to different environmental conditions and colonized diverse geographical regions over millions of years.
